So operation corresponds to a right rotation by l (where l in [1,n-1]), i.e., moving last l chars to front. Equivalent to left rotation by n-l (since moving suffix to front is left rotate by n-l?). Let's verify: left rotate by (n-l) yields: 'abcd' left rotate by 3 => 'dabc' which matches l=1 suffix move. left rotate by 2 => 'cdab' matches l=2 suffix move. So operation = left rotate by any amount from 1 to n-1 (excluding 0 and n). Actually l in [1,n-1]; left rotate by n-l where n-l in [1,n-1] also. So operation allowed: any non-zero rotation less than n (i.e., any rotation offset in [1, n-1]). So each operation picks an offset r in [1, n-1] and left-rotates s by r (or right rotates by l). That's the transformation.
